newsitem.title: UK: Guitarist Eric Clapton to sell art collection.
newsitem.headline: Guitarist Eric Clapton to sell art collection.

text.p: Legendary blues guitarist Eric Clapton is selling his collection of 20th century pictures, drawings and sculptures, auctioneers Christie's said on Wednesday.
The collection, with works from artists including Degas, Severini and Matisse, is expected to fetch up to 500,000 pounds ($822,000) when it goes under the hammer on May 29.

"As with his music Mr Clapton's taste is eclectic, highly personal and strongly rooted in tradition," Brett Gorvy, Christie's director of contemporary art said. "It has been assembled by someone who has not been affected by the vagaries of fashion."

Clapton, 52, is acknowledged as the world's greatest white blues guitarist who made his name playing in the "Yardbirds", "Cream", "Blind Faith" and "Derek & The Dominoes", but his art collection has been a well kept secret.

Among the works which will be sold are Le Sommeil, a pencil drawing by Edgar Degas that is expected to sell for up to 16,000 pounds ($26,000), Henri Matisse's Nu Debout and Maurice Utrillo's Le Bouquet.
The collection also includes pictures by Serge Poliakoff, one of the leading French abstract painters of the 1950s, and works by English artists Bridget Riley and Sir Matthew Smith.
